brief: Calmly receive a potentially embarrassing fact without collapsing, arguing, or performing dominance.

section: A good idea must be allowed to fail
line: A good idea must be allowed to fail.
brief: A real test has a visible path to failure; a protected idea is theater rather than inquiry.
Build with enough slack that one mistake, tired operator, failed tool, or bad assumption can be noticed and repaired instead of collapsing the whole effort.
A more capable machine reaches an independently controlled gate that can still refuse deployment; increased ability does not automatically widen authority.

section: Keep the stop path outside the failure
line: A stop button is only real if you can still reach it when things go wrong.
brief: Show an operator retaining a clear independent shutdown path while the main machine or interface becomes overloaded, noisy, or unstable.

line: Make intelligence abundant without making authority automatic.
brief: Many cheap machine-generated proposals multiply rapidly, while a separate narrow gate preserves deliberate judgment before consequential action.

section: This philosophy may also be wrong
line: Do not defend something merely because it is yours.
brief: Release attachment to one's own idea when reality supplies a better one.

section: Build tools that can disagree with you
line: Build tools that can say no to you.
brief: A useful instrument, experiment, friend, or computer can contradict its creator.

line: There is no special step called: Become defensive.
brief: When a claim arrives: yes if true, show why if false, test if uncertain, and continue.
